problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 0 \\ -8 & 9 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & a \\ 1 & 0 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the value of $a+2b.$
worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=8,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=9,\,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=10.$ 

So, the third column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}=10.$

Now, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{3}=10.$ Computing $A-10I,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-10I & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 0 \\ -8 & 9 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -8 & -1 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ that we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -8 & -1 & -3 & 0 \\ -8 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -8 & -1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=-{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{4}{x}_{3}.$ 
Hence, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4}{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=4,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a+2b=-4+2(4)=4.$
